description:
Parent: op-841p. THE RUNG 2 TO RUNG 3 INTERFACE. Wire to op-p6p.4 (genfoam neutronics/XS nuclearData structures, In Progress); do not invent a parallel format.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED IN THE CODE 2026-08-11 (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/genfoam/):
- The whole genfoam subtree is 32,334 lines with 262 tests and NOT ONE todo!().
- neutronics/xs/ (2167 lines, 13 tests): CrossSectionData at xs/mod.rs:134, NuclearDataOneEnergy at xs/nuclear_data_one_energy.rs:63.
- GroupConstants at xs/group_constants.rs:59 IS THE LANDING STRUCT and is already uom-typed: diffusion_coefficient (m), nu_sigma_f (1/m), sigma_pow (J/m), sigma_removal (1/m), chi_prompt, chi_delayed, inverse_velocity (s/m), disc_factor. PrecursorConstants at :85 carries beta, beta_tot, lambda.

THE HARD PART, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: GeN-Foam's nuclearData is NOT an njoy/OpenMC MGXS library. It is a dict PARAMETERISED BY FEEDBACK VARIABLES via polyharmonic-spline RBF interpolation across perturbed reactor states. So the bridge is not a format conversion - it is 'run rung 1 at N perturbed states (fuel temperature, moderator temperature, density) and fit the interpolant'. Design the perturbation matrix explicitly and record it in the run manifest.

HOMOGENISATION IS THE OTHER HALF, AND IT IS EXPENSIVE TO GET WRONG. Wang et al. (2014), Ann. Nucl. Energy 64, 1-7 (PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host) measured, against continuous-energy MCNP5 on the detailed HTR-10 model: INFHOMMEDIUM +2820 +/- 19 pcm, LATTICECELL +681 +/- 24, MULTIREGION +661 +/- 21, LATTICECELL(CELLMIX) +653 +/- 21, MULTIREGION(CELLMIX) +470 +/- 22, DOUBLEHET +276 +/- 20. Worst is 10.2x the best. A homogenised pebble-bed model cannot reach the ~200 pcm accuracy this benchmark needs - which is exactly why the rung 2->3 homogenisation must be MEASURED against rung 1, not assumed. Captured as typed data in outram_park_digital_twin_engine::htr10::neutronics::wang_2014_unit_cell_bias.
title: HTR-10 rung 2->3 seam: bridge MGXS into GeN-Foam nuclearData (RBF-parameterised over states)

description: Found 2026-08-11 by read-only correlation audit during op-4542; grouped low-severity items. (1) PipeConstantHeatFluxFullyDeveloped returns 4.354 at three sites in nusselt_number_correlations/enums.rs while its own doc says 4.36 and the free function laminar_nusselt_uniform_heat_flux_fully_developed returns 4.36; exact analytic value is 48/11 = 4.3636, and 4.354 is Gnielinski's blend fitting constant, not the fully-developed value. (2) PipeGnielinskiTurbulentPrandtlBulk documented 'only for turbulent flow in pipes' but dispatches to the interpolated laminar/transition/turbulent function. (3) PipeGnielinskiGenericPrandtlFilm no-wall-correction path calls the bulk-Prandtl function rather than the film one -- numerically identical there, cosmetic. (4) Gnielinski Pr upper bound allows 1e5 vs published 0.5<=Pr<=2000 (permissive, not wrong). (5) Five byte-identical hand-inlined copies of the CIET heater v2 Nusselt correlation in test files (single_control_vol/tests/conjugate_heat_transfer_tests/ciet_heater_v2_single_cv.rs:2265, _speedup_one_radial_steel_shell_node.rs:1071, _speedup_three_axial_nodes.rs:1201, _speedup_multithreading.rs:3137, pre_built_components/heat_transfer_entities/tests/mod.rs:789) -- all with correct exponents, but they will not track future library corrections. (6) insulated_pipes_and_fluid_components/tutorials/tutorial_6.rs:85-91 comment's pasted NIST citation lost superscript minus signs (T3 vs code's T^-3); code likely right, comment garbled.
title: tuas: minor correlation doc/code mismatches from op-4542 audit (4.354 vs 4.36, Gnielinski variant docs, inlined test copies)

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate initially**

**Do not represent all combustion exhaust as one generic anonymous sink. Track
source identity.**

Potential sources: FCC regenerator; Claus thermal stage; auxiliary
boilers/heaters; remaining fired equipment; coke combustion/gasification.

**A nuclear refinery should have substantially less routine furnace flue gas**
because HTGR process heat replaces many fired heaters -- which is precisely why
attributing flue gas to its source matters here more than in a conventional
refinery. An anonymous sink would hide the main benefit being claimed.

Cleanup may require: catalyst fines/PM; SOx; NOx; CO; CO2; oxygen; water;
eventual CO2 capture.

Scope **source-specific treatment trains**, not one universal scrubber.

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: Flue-gas cleanup with source identity

description:
Maintainer decision 2026-08-14, taken with the consequence stated. This script is the reproducibility artifact for the Annals of Nuclear Energy submission; its own docstring says it is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL with a twin in the paper's src/results_and_discussion/kloc_accounting/ 'so that diff is a sufficient check'.

THE CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED ONCE AND NOT RE-ARGUED: porting raises a journal reader's reproduction bar from 'python3 kloc_accounting.py' to 'build a 40-crate Rust workspace', and breaks the byte-identical diff with the manuscript. The maintainer was shown this and chose the full port anyway. Whoever does the work should make sure the manuscript side is updated in the same window, or the paper will cite a script that no longer exists.

WHAT IT DOES (1,454 lines, inventory taken 2026-08-14):
  Repo resolution + GitHub cloning   repo_url, find_repo, ensure_vendor, clone_missing, resolve  -- NETWORK
  Git archaeology                    git, ref_exists, select_ref, active_days, head_date
  Materialisation                    materialize -- git archive piped into tarfile extraction
  Line counting                      strip_rust_comments, rust_files, count_lines
  Measurement                        measure_repo, measure_baseline, measure_agentic, report_peak
  Console report                     report, fmt
  CSV output                         write_csvs -> baseline_repositories.csv, agentic_crates.csv
  LaTeX tables                       baseline_table_tex, rate_table_tex, agentic_table_tex, write_latex_tables
  Figure                             make_figure -> fig_kloc_productivity.png (matplotlib, Agg, 200 dpi)

PLACEMENT: kovan-metrics. It is repository accounting, which is exactly what that crate already does for 'kovan historian' and 'kovan tokens'. CLI surface as 'kovan kloc'.

FIGURE DECISION: emit hand-rolled SVG, not a raster PNG. No plotting crate is in [workspace.dependencies] and adding one buys a dependency whose font metrics and rasterisation vary by version -- the opposite of deterministic. The figure is two stacked horizontal bar charts with text labels and a light x-grid; that is straightforward SVG. Vector also suits a LaTeX manuscript better than a 200-dpi PNG. NOTE this visibly changes the artifact in the paper.

PARITY IS MANDATORY, per the 'no Python for docs or accounting' hard rule: run the Python FIRST, commit its CSV and .tex outputs, then port, then diff. op-yz7b shipped without a parity gate and that is recorded as a known weakness; do not repeat it. The figure cannot be diffed byte-for-byte across a format change -- compare the underlying numbers instead, and eyeball the rendering.

NETWORK CAVEAT: clone_missing fetches from GitHub. kovan is offline-by-charter, so the cloning path must be explicitly opt-in and desktop-scope, in kovan-cli rather than kovan-metrics -- the same split used for 'kovan setup' and 'kovan api-docs'.
title: Port kloc_accounting.py to kovan and delete it (~1450 lines; paper reproducibility artifact)
